text:
Maya: customer (acme-inc) hit a bad case — their refund call ended up routed to invoice_lookup and the user was charged instead of refunded. request_id=req_0x9a7f, customer upset. Can we triage?

Devon: ugh. do we have the original request payload / model response? need model name + any function call the model returned.

Maya: pasting the payload they sent and the returned function call from our logs:
```json
{\n  \"user_id\": \"acct_acme\",\n  \"prompt\": \"Customer says they were double-charged, please refund $45.00 to card on file.\",\n  \"model\": \"open-llm-4-medium\",\n  \"tools_allowed\": [\"refund_processor\", \"invoice_lookup\"],\n  \"metadata\": {}\n}
```
and model/function response captured in runtime logs:
```json
{\n  \"function_call\": {\n    \"name\": \"invoice_lookup\",\n    \"arguments\": { \"invoice_id\": \"inv_12345\" }\n  },\n  \"text\": \"Looks like this charge comes from invoice inv_12345.\"\n}
```

Samir: thanks. router logs show the model returned invoice_lookup. score breakdown: invoice_lookup=0.62, refund_processor=0.61 — basically a tie. both tools have nearly identical argument schemas: {amount, currency, reason} in one variant and {invoice_id} in the other, but our schema normalization collapses optional fields and made them look similar for the resolver.

infra-bot: log snippet (router) req=req_0x9a7f, model=open-llm-4-medium, tool_candidates=[invoice_lookup,refund_processor], chosen=invoice_lookup, reason=ambiguous_signature_similarity, selection_delta=0.01

Lia: that explains it. these misroutes happen when two tool names overlap semantically and model latent preference nudges it the other way. propose short-term: 1) allow callers to pass explicit function_call preference or \"preferred_tool\" metadata 2) add a disambiguating required enum field (operation: [\"charge\",\"refund\"]) to refund_processor schema so resolver has a stronger signal.

Devon: agree. can we reproduce locally? Samir, can you share a curl repro that support can run?

Samir: yes, here's a minimal curl that reproduces the misroute against staging (note: model is probabilistic, may need a couple tries):
```bash
curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{\n  "model":"open-llm-4-medium",\n  "input":"please refund $45 to the customer card on file",\n  "tools_allowed":["refund_processor","invoice_lookup"],\n  "temperature":0.6\n}'
```
It will often return a function_call named invoice_lookup.

Maya: support tried the curl and hit it twice in a row. both misrouted. customer is asking for ETA on a fix — we should escalate.

Devon: short-term mitigation for customer: call the refund_processor ourselves from the support backend (bypass resolver) using internal service credentials. will need approval from payments (fraud check).

Samir: I opened ENG-ML ticket ENG-ML-1023 and assigned to @devon and @lia. proposal in ticket: (A) change resolver scoring to include semantic token check for keywords (refund/refund_amount/refund) with +0.2 bias for matching tool names, (B) enforce stricter schema fingerprinting so overlapping optional fields don't collapse, (C) add API flag allow_explicit_tool to let callers force tool.

Lia: also adding a model-side guard: if user intent text contains the word \"refund\", prioritize refund_processor. quick rule can drop incidents.

Devon: will draft a short support KB entry: how to force tool selection via metadata (workaround) + automated detection. Maya, can you ask customer if they want an immediate manual refund while eng-ml works the fix?

Maya: i'll ask and tell them we can do a manual refund today. also flagged billing ops to reconcile.

infra-bot: ticket ENG-ML-1023 created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ENG-ML-1023 — summary: tool_router misroutes refund -> invoice_lookup due to ambiguous schema; priority=high

Samir: next steps: 1) eng-ml implements schema disambiguation + keyword bias (short spike, 2–3 days) 2) add API metadata for explicit preferred_tool (hotfix) 3) support KB & manual refund for the customer.

Devon: assigning follow-ups: @lia to spike keyword bias + KB, @samir to API flag PR, @maya to customer comms and manual refund coord.

Maya: will update thread after confirm with customer. :white_check_mark:

Lia: adding if anyone else sees similar misroutes, drop examples here with request_id so we can group them in ENG-ML-1023.

Devon: thanks team. :thumbsup:
